daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Indonesian Solidarity Party (PSI) is launching an ambitious grassroots campaign as it targets a top-three finish in future elections, instructing cadres to descend to the community level. Political observers warn that PSI needs strong grassroots machinery and cannot rely solely on Jokowi's appeal, with the party itself acknowledging it wants to produce new "Jokowi figures" from among its own cadres. PSI's Bogor branch jokingly asked when the former president would formally join the party structure.

  • Nahdlatul Ulama's new leadership under Gus Kikin is beginning its term, with consolidation and programs under scrutiny as Gus Kikin explained considerations behind the composition of PBNU's 2026–2031 leadership structure.
  • PBNU Secretary-General Gus Ipul said that PCNU Nias has not clarified the handover of Rp 250 million to the KPK.
  • Vice President Ma'ruf Amin provided compensation to forest fire volunteers in South Kalimantan.
  • Minister of State Secretary Yusril Ihza Mahendra was invited by the National Energy Council, raising speculation about whether his proposal to change the legal definition of corruption will be discussed.
  • The Minister of Home Affairs instructed local governments to allocate budgets for renovating uninhabitable homes, saying the state wants to address root problems in kampungs through housing renovation programs.
  • Analysis notes weak points in the narrative surrounding Deputy Minister Stella's "not resilient" controversy.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia is chairing the Counter-Terrorism Information Facility (CTIF) in Singapore, strengthening regional anti-terrorism cooperation. Former TNI Commander Admiral Widodo AS, the first Navy officer to serve as TNI chief, has passed away, with Lieutenant General Suryo Prabowo sharing memories of the late admiral. Indonesia continues its humanitarian engagement in the Middle East by delivering clean water to nearly 7,000 people in Gaza.

  • Indonesia and Australia are partnering to protect children in the digital space and pushing for regional cooperation against transnational crime.
  • The Indonesian government confirmed Indonesians were injured during Typhoon Champi in Taiwan, with follow-up on the condition of Indonesian nationals there, and the Foreign Ministry monitoring the safety of Indonesians after an earthquake in Tibet.
  • A total of 136 TNI soldiers in Papua received extraordinary promotions for safeguarding national unity.
  • Bali and Timor-Leste are exploring a deal for cattle exports from the neighboring country.

Other

Indonesia has launched rice assistance for 33.2 million beneficiaries in a major social protection initiative. Meanwhile, Indonesia has slashed gas exports to Singapore, with Singapore acknowledging the impact on its energy security. Data from BPS shows 9.29 million households lack homes while 18 million live in uninhabitable dwellings.

  • Market analysts have offered advice to the government on fixing the stock market following the MSCI controversy.
  • The Danantara forum is seeking global investment in Indonesia's technology sector, while a minister said Indonesia aims to expand digital jobs through animation.
  • The Ministry of Environment plans to expand producer responsibility for plastic waste management.
  • Indonesia released two orangutans into the wild in West Kalimantan as part of conservation efforts.
  • Aviation fuel prices have reached US$206 per barrel, creating pressure expected to continue through 2027.
